conbody.p: In Impala, query execution always starts from scratch, computing intermediate results in several stages to produce the final results. These intermediate results are discarded at the end of query execution, so the computation must be repeated for a new run of the query even if none of the underlying data has changed. Caching intermediate results can improve the latency for repetitive work while also freeing up resources for other queries.

section.title: Basic Configuration
section.p:
The intermediate results cache is enabled via the following configurations:
--allow_tuple_caching is a startup flag that gates the intermediate results caching feature. It must be set to true on coordinators and executors to allow the use of the intermediate results cache, but it does not enable the cache by itself.
The --tuple_cache startup flag specifies the storage directory and quota for the intermediate results cache on coordinators and executors. The flag is set to a directory name followed by a : and a capacity for that directory. For example: --tuple_cache=/data/cache:20GB This setting uses the /data/cache directory and allows the cache to consume up to 20GB in that directory. The directory must exist in the local filesystem of each Impala Daemon, or Impala will fail to start.
The enable_tuple_cache query option determines whether a query uses the intermediate results cache. To use the feature, this must be set to true via the session or default_query_options.
All three of these settings must be specified to use the intermediate results cache. The default value for all three configurations is for the feature to be disabled.

The cache key incorporates information about all the settings that can impact the query results, including information about the base tables and any query options. When any of those settings change, it results in a new cache entry. For example, if new data is ingested into a base table, the key will change. This means that there is no need for an administrator to manually refresh or invalidate the cache entries.

When the cache reaches the quota, cache entries are evicted to make space for new entries. The cache eviction policy can be specified by the --tuple_cache_eviction_policy startup flag. Currently, the cache supports the following cache eviction policies:
LRU (Least Recently Used--the default)
LIRS (Least Inter-reference Recency Set)
LIRS is a scan-resistant, low performance-overhead policy.

section.title: Eligible Locations in the Plan
section.p: The intermediate results cache stores the output of a node in the query plan, so a cache lookup can replace the work of everything below that node, including work in other fragments. A location in the plan is eligible for caching only if its output is fully determined by its cache key. If Impala cannot guarantee that, a cache hit could return stale or incorrect results, so the location is not eligible.

A location is ineligible for one of two basic reasons:
Non-deterministic behavior: The subtree can produce different results for the same inputs. For example, it calls a non-deterministic function such as RAND(), or it contains a LIMIT, which may return a different set of rows on each run.
Unsupported functionality: The subtree uses a feature that the cache does not yet support, such as full ACID tables or exchanges that merge or repartition rows.
Ineligibility propagates up the plan: if any child of a node is ineligible, the node is also ineligible. Eligibility is only a prerequisite. Impala chooses which of the eligible locations to actually cache as described in the next section.

To see why a location is ineligible, run EXPLAIN with the EXPLAIN_LEVEL query option set to VERBOSE while enable_tuple_cache is true. Each plan node reports either its cost information or a "tuple cache ineligibility reasons" line.

section.title: Cost-Based Placement
section.p:
Impala does not cache at every eligible location. Caching has overhead when a result is written, and a cache entry is only valuable if reading it is much cheaper than recomputing it. Instead, Impala uses the estimated processing cost of the plan to choose a subset of eligible locations in three steps:
Threshold: Locations are discarded if the cost of reading the result from the cache is not sufficiently lower than the cost of computing it. The tuple_cache_required_cost_reduction_factor query option sets the threshold. A location is considered only if the cost of computing the result is at least this many times the cost of reading it from the cache. The default is 3.0, meaning that reading from the cache must cost less than 1/3 of computing the result. A higher value caches less aggressively and lowers the overhead.
Ranking: The remaining locations are ranked by the cost reduction per byte of cache space: (cost of regular execution - cost of reading from the cache) / estimated serialized size This favors locations with small results or a large reduction in cost.
Budget: Locations are picked in rank order until the budget for the estimated serialized size per executor is used up. A location that does not fit in the remaining budget is skipped, but smaller locations ranked below it can still be picked. The tuple_cache_budget_bytes_per_executor query option sets the budget. It accepts a memory specification such as 200MB, and the default is 100MB. A higher value caches more aggressively, which can increase the overhead the first time a query runs. A lower value limits the overhead at the expense of less caching. The budget is per executor, so the total scales with the number of executors.
For example: SET enable_tuple_cache=true; SET tuple_cache_required_cost_reduction_factor=5; SET tuple_cache_budget_bytes_per_executor=200MB;
Because the estimates depend on table and column statistics, run COMPUTE STATS on the tables in queries that use the cache.

When EXPLAIN_LEVEL is VERBOSE, the explain plan shows the estimated serialized size, the cumulative processing cost, and the cache read and write processing costs for each eligible location. This can help explain why a particular location was or was not picked.

section.title: Monitoring Cache Hits and Misses
section.p:
Each cached location in a query appears as a TUPLE_CACHE_NODE in the query profile. The following counters on that node show what happened for each fragment instance:
NumTupleCacheHits is 1 if the result was read from the cache. If it is 0, the result was a cache miss and was computed normally.
NumTupleCacheSkipped is 1 if there was a miss and the result was not written to the cache. This happens if another fragment is already writing the same entry, or if the entry was previously found to be too large.
NumTupleCacheHalted and NumTupleCacheBackpressureHalted are 1 if writing the result to the cache was abandoned, either because the entry exceeded the maximum entry size or because too many cache writes were outstanding.
The Combined Key info string on the node shows the cache key for that fragment instance.

Each Impala daemon also keeps cumulative statistics for its cache in the impala.tuple-cache.* metrics, such as impala.tuple-cache.hits, impala.tuple-cache.misses, and impala.tuple-cache.entries-evicted. These metrics are on the Metrics page of the Impala daemon debug web UI. See for details about the web UI.
